Torrent bonding you can trust on a phone tether:

- An uplink must pass a live probe before it is used, and one that stops
  passing is dropped: a tethered phone that keeps its adapter up while the data
  connection is gone no longer swallows half the peer connections.
- New peer connections are weighted by the bytes each uplink actually delivers
  (IPv6 included), so a link that degrades to a crawl stops getting swarm.
- Bonding follows the machine: plug the phone in, or toggle it in Settings, and
  torrents pick it up without restarting the daemon.

GUI fixes and quality-of-life:

- The row context menu works again (clicking an entry's icon or label did
  nothing), and a paused row has its Resume button back.
- Paused and finished rows no longer show a phantom download rate.
- Multi-select with Ctrl/Shift-click or Ctrl+A for bulk pause/resume/remove;
  removing an unfinished task asks first.
- A download being set up reads "connecting" instead of running at 0 B/s.
- View > Peers column (off by default) and "Copy address" in the row menu.
